To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oceanic islands are exceptionally vulnerable to problems associated both with the coast and with the environment as a whole, and that their sustainable management requires a comprehensive understanding of the processes and interactions involved.

oceanic islands are particularly vulnerable to environmental change and that the sustainable management of oceanic island coastlines requires a thorough understanding of the nature of the island environment, the human and non-human drivers of change, and the role of the international community in the sustainable development of these islands.

(1) oceanic islands are vulnerable to coastal problems; (2) the sustainable management of the coasts of oceanic islands is an essential prerequisite for their sustainable development; (3) sustainable development of the coasts is a key issue for the future of many island nations; and (4) sustainable management is threatened by a lack of knowledge and understanding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and extent of the problems associated with the sustainable management of the coasts of oceanic islands.
the sustainable management of oceanic island environments.
the future of the world's islands and the role of coastal processes and management in their survival.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the future of ocean island coasts is bleak, unless the human inhabitants can learn to live with nature rather than against it.

the future of the human populations of many island states is intrinsically linked to the sustainable management of coasts, a task which is becoming increasingly difficult as island populations grow and the demands placed on island coasts change and intensify.

island coasts are a unique and important resource that are under threat from a variety of natural and anthropogenic processes, and that the future of the people who inhabit these coasts depends upon their ability to manage them in a sustainable way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
island coasts, and the human communities that depend on them, are vulnerable to the same problems that affect continental coasts but to a greater degree.

island coasts are highly vulnerable to environmental change and that the human inhabitants of these islands must be prepared to adapt their lifestyles and management practices in order to maintain a sustainable future.

the sustainable development of oceanic island coastlines depends on an integrated approach that combines a detailed understanding of island coasts and their environments with a commitment to the development of appropriate management strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the future of the human populations of most oceanic islands depends intrinsically upon the sustainable management of the coasts of those islands.

the future of island coasts depends on the development of a more holistic approach to their sustainable management that takes into account the complex interactions between human activities, island ecosystems, and the physical processes that shape island coasts.
the future of ocean islands is inextricably linked to the future of the world's oceans.
